title: Scale Labs: Commitment Curation and Dedicated Autoscale Playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a repeatable quarterly playbook and experiment templates for running scale labs that validate reservation commitment sizes, pre-warm strategies, and adaptive autoscale policies for Dedicated pools. Outcome: a tested set of experiments, a decision rubric for commitment sizing, and an ops playbook (runbook + dashboards) to reduce wasted reservation spend while meeting P95 latency and throughput SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook with step-by-step experiment templates (3 templated scenarios: conservative-commit, hybrid-commit, thin-commit + burst) published in Confluence
Decision rubric that maps workload telemetry (QPS distribution, tail latency, cold-start frequency) to recommended commitment size and autoscale guardrails
Three completed scale-lab experiments across customer-like workloads with recorded metrics: cost/unit, P95 latency, failed requests
Dashboard tile in Console showing projected reservation utilization and recommended reserve adjustments
Hand-off doc and on-call checklist for Dedicated SREs for graceful fastpath/hedged autoscale during surges
updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with Eng (SRE + Runtime) and Design. Agreed scope: templated experiments + runbook + dashboard mockups.
2025-02-21: Eng provided initial telemetry samples from 3 customer workloads (search, chat assistant, batch-embed). Need to synthesize QPS/slice distributions.
2025-02-25: Decision to prioritize 'hybrid-commit' scenario first (partial reservation + burst reservoir) due to highest ROI signal on telemetry.
2025-02-28: Design review feedback: simplify experiment matrix to 4 axes (commit %, prewarm window, burst cap, priority fanout). Follow-up: add explicit rollback criteria.
2025-03-03: Draft Confluence playbook uploaded (link below). Small pilot scheduled for 2025-03-10 on staging dedicated pool.
2025-03-04: PM note - raised risk that current autoscale controller doesn't expose per-customer cost projection; dependency ENG-19877 created to add cost hooks.
next_steps: Complete pilot run on staging pools (2025-03-10 to 2025-03-14) and collect cost/latency traces
Iterate runbook based on pilot findings; add explicit SLO degradation thresholds and rollback tranche
Finalize dashboard mockups and open ticket for Console to implement projection tiles (ENG-20230)
Schedule cross-functional review (PM/Eng/Design/SRE) 2025-03-18 to sign off playbook
decision_log: 2025-02-21: Use three customer workload templates rather than five to reduce noise in early experiments
2025-02-25: Prioritize hybrid-commit scenario (partial reservation + burst) for first pilot due to highest projected cost savings
2025-02-28: Limit experiment horizon to two weeks per cohort to bound spend and speed iteration
rollout_calendar: Pilot (staging) 2025-03-10 to 2025-03-14; Canary (selected customers on dedicated) 2025-03-25 to 2025-04-05; Full playbook publish 2025-04-15
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive downscale reduces wasted reservation but risks increased cold-start latency; mitigation: prewarm windows sized from observed KV cache access patterns.
Design requested visual examples of 'commitment slider' for Console UX to illustrate marginal cost benefit; DES-501 will deliver comps.
Finance requested an expected cost delta model attached to final decision rubric to support sales conversations for reserved contracts.
